_meta.feast: The Nativity of Our Most Holy Lady, the Theotokos and Ever-Virgin Mary
_meta._note: Single-canon (1st Canon Tone 2 by John of Damascus) with Tone 8 Katavasiae from the Canon of the Elevation of the Cross (Aug 6 → Sep 14 katavasiae cycle). Only the 2nd Exapostilarion (festal) is given; the 1st would be resurrectional and is omitted on weekday Theotokos feasts. Magnificat replaced by feast-specific Ode 9 refrain (`skipMagnificat: true`).

troparion.text:
Thy nativity, O Virgin,
has proclaimed joy to the whole universe!
The Sun of righteousness, Christ our God,
has shone from thee, O Theotokos.
By annulling the curse,
He bestowed a blessing.
By destroying death, He has granted us eternal life.
troparion.label: Troparion of the Nativity of the Theotokos

kontakion.text:
By thy nativity, O most pure Virgin,
Joachim and Anna are freed from barrenness,
Adam and Eve — from the corruption of death.
And we, thy people, freed from the guilt of sin, celebrate and sing to thee:
"The barren woman gives birth to the Theotokos, the nourisher of our Life."
kontakion.label: Kontakion of the Nativity of the Theotokos

magnification.refrain:
We magnify thee,
O Most-Holy Virgin,
and we honor thy holy parents
and praise thine all-glorious nativity.
verses: O Lord, remember David and all his meekness. (Ps. 131:1)
Arise, O Lord, into Thy rest; Thou and the Ark of Thy Holiness. (Ps. 131:8)

prokeimenon.refrain: I will remember thy name from generation to generation.
prokeimenon.verse: My heart overflowed with a good word.

gospel._note: The Visitation — Mary visits Elizabeth. "My soul magnifies the Lord…"

postGospelSticheron.text:
This is the day of the Lord!
Rejoice, O peoples,
for, behold, the bridal chamber of the Light, the book of the Word of Life,
has come forth from the womb!
The gate that faces the East is born
and awaits the entry of the Great Priest.
She alone admits Christ into the world
for the salvation of our souls.
postGospelSticheron.label: Idiomelon of the Nativity of the Theotokos

canon._katavasiaeNote: Katavasiae Tone 8 from the Canon of the Elevation of the Cross (by Cosmas the Monk), per the Aug 6 → Sep 14 cycle.

ode1.irmos:
Come, O peoples, let us sing a song to Christ our God
Who parted the sea and through it led His people,
whom He had brought out of bondage in Egypt;
for He has been glorified!
ode1.katavasia:
Moses traced out a cross,
as with his staff he divided the Red Sea in two,
so that Israel could go across on foot;
and then striking it again crosswise,
and uniting it over Pharaoh and his chariots,
he inscribed the Invincible Weapon.
Therefore let us sing to Christ our God, for He has been glorified.

ode3.irmos:
Establish us in Thyself, O Lord;
Thou Who on the Tree didst put sin to death,
and implant the fear of Thee in the hearts
of us who sing praises to Thee.
ode3.katavasia:
The rod of Aaron is an image of this mystery,
for when it budded it revealed who should be the priest;
and for the Church, which before was barren,
the Tree of the Cross has blossomed forth
for her strength and firm foundation.

ode4.irmos:
I have heard, O Lord, the report of Thy dispensation,
and I have glorified Thee,
the only Lover of mankind.
ode4.katavasia:
I have heard the mystery of Thy dispensation, O Lord,
I have meditated on Thy works
and have glorified Thy Godhead.

ode5.irmos:
Thou hast dispelled the mist of dark sayings obscurely worded,
and hast illumined the hearts of the faithful
by the fulfillment of the truth through the Maiden of God;
guide us also by Thy light, O Christ!
ode5.katavasia:
O thrice-blessed Tree, on which Christ the King and Lord was stretched!
Through thee the one who deceived us through a tree has fallen,
caught by the bait of God, Who was nailed to thee in the flesh,
and Who grants peace to our souls.

ode6.irmos:
From within the belly of the whale Jonah cried to the Lord:
"Lead me up, I pray Thee, from the depths of hell,
that with a voice of praise
and in the Spirit of truth
I may sacrifice to Thee as my Deliverer!"
ode6.katavasia:
In the belly of the sea monster, Jonah stretched out his hands in the form of a cross,
plainly prefiguring the saving Passion.
When he emerged from there on the third day,
he prefigured the transcendent Resurrection of Christ our God,
Who was nailed to the Cross in the flesh
and by His rising on the third day enlightened the world.

ode7.irmos:
The bush on the mountain unconsumed by fire
and the Chaldean furnace that shed dew
plainly prefigured thee, the Bride of God,
for thou didst receive, without being consumed,
the divine and immaterial Fire in a material womb.
Therefore, we cry to Him Who was born of thee:
"Blessed art Thou, the God of our Fathers!"
ode7.katavasia:
The senseless decree of the impious tyrant,
spewing threats and blasphemy hateful to God,
brought the people to confusion.
Yet the three Children could not be frightened
either by the brutal fury or the roaring fire,
but in the wind, moist with dew, that blew against it,
they stood together, and they sang:
"O praised above all, blessed art Thou,
our God, and the God of our Fathers!"

ode8.irmos:
In the furnace of the Children,
once Thou didst prefigure Thine own Mother, O Lord;
and this type delivered them from the fire
as they walked in the midst of it unconsumed.
To her do we sing praises
as Thou hast manifested her today to the ends of the earth,
and we exalt her above all forever.
ode8.katavasia:
O Children, equal in number to the Trinity,
bless God the Father, the Creator;
praise the Word, Who descended and changed the fire to dew,
and exalt above all, to all ages,
the All-Holy Spirit, Who gives life to all!

ode9.irmos:
Refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the most glorious birth of the Mother of God!

Heirmos: From thy virgin womb thou ineffably gavest a body
to the Light that was before the sun,
even God Who has shone forth upon us,
and in the body came to dwell among us.
Blessed and all-pure Theotokos, we magnify thee!
ode9.katavasia:
Thou art a mystical Paradise, O Theotokos,
who, though untilled, hast brought forth Christ;
through Him the life-bearing wood of the Cross was planted on earth.
Now at its Exaltation,
as we bow in worship before it, we magnify thee.

exapostilarion.text:
Be renewed, O Adam, and be magnified, O Eve,
you prophets dance with the apostles and the righteous;
let there be common joy in the world among angels and mankind.
For the Theotokos is born today of righteous Joachim and Anna.
exapostilarion.label: 2nd Exapostilarion of the Nativity of the Theotokos

stichera.verse: Praise Him for His mighty deeds; praise Him according to His exceeding greatness! (Ps. 150:2)
stichera.text:
Oh, the marvelous wonder!
The source of Life is born of a barren woman,
and grace gloriously begins to bear its fruit.
Rejoice, Joachim, who have become the father of the Theotokos!
There is no other like thee among earthborn fathers, O man inspired by God;
for the Maiden in whom God would come to dwell,
the Tabernacle of God, the all-holy Mountain,
has been given to us through thee.

stichera.verse: Praise Him with trumpet sound; praise Him with lute and harp! (Ps. 150:3)
Praise Him with timbrel and dance; praise Him with strings and pipe! (Ps. 150:4)
stichera.text:
Oh, the marvelous wonder!
The fruit of a barren woman
has shone forth at the behest of the Almighty Maker of all
and mightily destroyed the barrenness of this world, which was fruitless in good things.
You mothers, dance with the mother of the Theotokos and cry:
"Rejoice, O Full of Grace, the Lord is with thee,
He Who grants the world through thee His great mercy!"

stichera.verse: Praise Him with sounding cymbals; praise Him with loud clashing cymbals! Let everything that breathes praise the Lord! (Ps. 150:5)
stichera.text:
A living pillar of chastity
and bright vessel shining with grace,
glorious Anna has given birth to the true stronghold of virginity,
the divine flower, who manifestly bestows the beauty of virginity
on all virgins and women who desire that grace,
and grants to all the faithful great mercy.
